issuing_body: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
title: Minnesota Medicaid Fraud Control Unit - 2026 Recertification Letter
supports: HHS-OIG conditionally recertified the Minnesota MFCU beginning 2026-07-01, subject to special corrective conditions.
OIG determined the Unit generally complied with applicable laws, regulations, and policy transmittals but was not adhering to all MFCU Performance Standards and needed additional action.
For FY2025, Minnesota MFCU reported 32 approved staff positions, 31 filled; OIG estimated approximately 41 staff based on Minnesota Medicaid expenditures of $21.4 billion.
The Unit reported that the May 2026 Legislature approved 18 additional positions: nine investigators, four attorneys, two auditors, and three support staff.

PIU/MCO referrals rose from 119 in FY2025 to nearly 790 between 2025-10-01 and 2026-05-14; the Unit reported quality decreased for many referrals, especially PIU referrals with limited preliminary analysis or information.
OIG found case progression effective; approximately 24 percent of open cases were more than three years old.
The Unit reported 30 open joint investigations with HHS-OIG's Office of Investigations.
OIG identified FY2024/FY2025 fiscal-control issues including late deliverables and an FY2025 Federal-grant 'overmatch' that the Unit attributed to staffing changes and turnover.

Minnesota MFCU reported 36 fraud convictions in FY2025, 115 fraud convictions over three years, 187 fraud investigations, 49 fraud indictments, 8 civil settlements and judgments, and more than $24 million in total monetary recoveries in FY2025.
OIG found Minnesota MFCU effective in investigating/prosecuting Medicaid fraud but said it should obtain law-enforcement authority to improve operational effectiveness.
OIG found the Unit was not using its resources effectively enough for patient-abuse/neglect matters; it reported two such convictions, 15 investigations, and one indictment in FY2025.
Special conditions require a fiscal-management corrective plan/progress report and implementation of the remaining 2022 inspection recommendation for a comprehensive case-management system.

money.notes: Minnesota MFCU annual-statistical-report figure quoted by HHS-OIG as total monetary recoveries. Do not combine with DHS identified-for-recovery or individual restitution figures without determining overlap.

important_qualifications: Conditional recertification is an administrative determination, not a criminal finding against MFCU staff.
The $24M figure is a Unit-reported annual recovery measure quoted by HHS-OIG; it may include multiple criminal/civil recovery types and should not be treated as one cash-restitution category.
Do not import the seven recommendation statuses numbered 26-E-07-010 from HHS-OIG's tracker into Minnesota; those belong to the Oklahoma MFCU 2025 inspection.
locators: letter pp.5-6 patient abuse and special conditions
